concepts.name: Tawhid (divine oneness)
concepts.definition: The doctrine of God's absolute unity and the rejection of any partner or division in His essence.
concepts.notes: Foundational doctrine whose interpretation divides every kalam school.

concepts.name: Tawhid al-uluhiyya (oneness of worship)
concepts.definition: The Atharist division asserting God alone deserves worship, distinct from oneness of lordship.

concepts.name: Tawhid al-rububiyya (oneness of lordship)
concepts.definition: Affirmation that God alone creates, sustains, and governs the cosmos.

concepts.name: Tawhid al-asma wa'l-sifat (oneness of names and attributes)
concepts.definition: Affirming God's revealed names and attributes without distortion, denial, or anthropomorphism.

concepts.name: Sifat Allah (divine attributes)
concepts.definition: Whether God's attributes are real, identical to His essence, or merely names.

concepts.name: Tashbih (anthropomorphism)
concepts.definition: Likening God to creation, especially regarding hands, face, or throne.

concepts.name: Tanzih (divine transcendence)
concepts.definition: Affirming God's absolute incomparability with creation.

concepts.name: Ta'til (divestment of attributes)
concepts.definition: Negating God's attributes entirely, attributed polemically to Jahmiyya and extreme Mu'tazila.

concepts.name: Ta'wil (allegorical interpretation)
concepts.definition: Interpreting ambiguous scriptural verses about God figuratively rather than literally.

concepts.name: Tafwid (consigning meaning to God)
concepts.definition: Affirming ambiguous attribute verses while delegating their true meaning to God.

concepts.name: Bila kayf (without asking how)
concepts.definition: Affirming divine attributes literally while refusing to specify modality.

concepts.name: Qadar (divine decree)
concepts.definition: Whether human actions are predetermined by God or freely chosen.

concepts.name: Jabr (compulsion)
concepts.definition: The position that humans are wholly compelled by God with no real agency.

concepts.name: Kasb (acquisition)
concepts.definition: Ash'ari doctrine that God creates acts which humans 'acquire' to ground responsibility.

concepts.name: Ikhtiyar (human choice)
concepts.definition: Affirmation of genuine human volition as the basis of moral accountability.

concepts.name: Istita'a (capacity to act)
concepts.definition: Whether human capacity to act exists before, during, or only with the action.

concepts.name: Khalq al-af'al (creation of acts)
concepts.definition: Whether God creates human acts or humans originate them independently.

concepts.name: Khalq al-Qur'an (createdness of the Qur'an)
concepts.definition: Whether the Qur'an is God's eternal speech or a created entity in time.
concepts.notes: Center of the mihna inquisition under the Abbasids.

concepts.name: Kalam Allah (divine speech)
concepts.definition: Distinction between God's eternal inner speech and its created verbal expression.

concepts.name: Ru'yat Allah (beatific vision)
concepts.definition: Whether believers will literally see God in the hereafter.

concepts.name: Husn wa qubh (moral ontology)
concepts.definition: Whether good and evil are intrinsic to acts or determined solely by revelation.

concepts.name: Al-aslah (the optimal)
concepts.definition: Mu'tazili principle that God must do what is best for His servants.

concepts.name: Lutf (divine grace)
concepts.definition: Acts of divine assistance that bring humans nearer to obedience without compulsion.
concepts.notes: Central to Twelver justification of the imamate.

concepts.name: Adl (divine justice)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that God acts only justly and cannot will evil.

concepts.name: Al-wa'd wa'l-wa'id (promise and threat)
concepts.definition: God's binding promise of reward and threat of punishment without remission.

concepts.name: Al-manzila bayna al-manzilatayn (intermediate position)
concepts.definition: Mu'tazili doctrine that the grave sinner is neither believer nor unbeliever.

concepts.name: Al-amr bi'l-ma'ruf wa'l-nahy 'an al-munkar
concepts.definition: The theological obligation to command right and forbid wrong.

concepts.name: Iman and amal (faith and works)
concepts.definition: Whether faith includes actions or is purely inner assent.

concepts.name: Irja (postponement of judgment)
concepts.definition: Deferring judgment on grave sinners to God and excluding works from faith's definition.

concepts.name: Takfir (excommunication)
concepts.definition: Conditions under which a Muslim may be declared an unbeliever.

concepts.name: Al-kabira (grave sin)
concepts.definition: Whether committing a major sin removes a Muslim from the faith.

concepts.name: Shafa'a (intercession)
concepts.definition: Whether prophets and saints can intercede for sinners on judgment day.

concepts.name: 'Isma (prophetic and imami infallibility)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that prophets and Shia imams are protected from sin and error.

concepts.name: Nubuwwa (prophethood)
concepts.definition: Rational and scriptural proofs for the necessity and authenticity of prophethood.

concepts.name: Khatm al-nubuwwa (finality of prophethood)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that Muhammad is the last prophet and no prophet will follow.

concepts.name: Mu'jiza (prophetic miracle)
concepts.definition: Evidentiary miracles that authenticate prophetic claims.

concepts.name: I'jaz al-Qur'an (Qur'anic inimitability)
concepts.definition: The miraculous, inimitable nature of the Qur'an as proof of its divine origin.

concepts.name: Sarfa (divine deflection)
concepts.definition: View that the Qur'an's inimitability comes from God preventing imitation, not the text itself.

concepts.name: Karamat al-awliya (saintly miracles)
concepts.definition: Whether non-prophets such as Sufi saints can perform genuine miracles.

concepts.name: Imama (Shia imamate)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that leadership after the Prophet is divinely appointed through Ali and his descendants.

concepts.name: Nass (designation)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that each imam is explicitly designated by his predecessor.

concepts.name: Ghayba (occultation)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that the twelfth imam is hidden and will return as Mahdi.

concepts.name: Raj'a (return)
concepts.definition: Belief that certain imams and companions will return to earth before judgment.

concepts.name: Bada' (divine alteration)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that God may alter what appeared to be His decree without contradiction.

concepts.name: Taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation)
concepts.definition: Concealing one's beliefs under threat of persecution.

concepts.name: Wilayat al-faqih (guardianship of the jurist)
concepts.definition: Theological-political doctrine of the jurist's authority during the imam's occultation.

concepts.name: Mahdi (eschatological guide)
concepts.definition: The awaited rightly-guided figure who restores justice before the end of time.

concepts.name: Dajjal (antichrist)
concepts.definition: Eschatological deceiver whose appearance signals the final hour.

concepts.name: Barzakh (intermediate realm)
concepts.definition: The state of souls between death and resurrection.

concepts.name: 'Adhab al-qabr (punishment in the grave)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that the dead experience reward or punishment before resurrection.

concepts.name: Ma'ad jismani (bodily resurrection)
concepts.definition: Whether resurrection is physical, spiritual, or both.

concepts.name: Hashr (gathering and judgment)
concepts.definition: The final assembly of all creation before God for reckoning.

concepts.name: Mizan (the scale)
concepts.definition: The eschatological balance weighing deeds on judgment day.

concepts.name: Sirat (the bridge)
concepts.definition: The bridge over hellfire crossed on the day of judgment.

concepts.name: Khulud (eternity of hell)
concepts.definition: Whether punishment in hell is everlasting or eventually ends.

concepts.name: Fitra (innate disposition)
concepts.definition: The natural human disposition toward recognizing God.

concepts.name: Al-mithaq (primordial covenant)
concepts.definition: The pre-eternal covenant in which souls testified to God's lordship.

concepts.name: Hudus al-'alam (temporal origination of the world)
concepts.definition: Whether the universe came into being in time or is eternal.

concepts.name: Qidam al-'alam (eternity of the world)
concepts.definition: Philosophical position that the cosmos is eternal alongside God.

concepts.name: Dalil al-huduth (argument from origination)
concepts.definition: Kalam proof for God from the temporal origin of the world.

concepts.name: Atomism (jawhar fard)
concepts.definition: Kalam metaphysics holding that bodies consist of indivisible atoms continually recreated by God.

concepts.name: Occasionalism
concepts.definition: Doctrine that God is the sole real cause and creates all events at every moment.

concepts.name: Sababiyya (secondary causality)
concepts.definition: Whether created causes have real efficacy or are mere occasions for divine action.

concepts.name: Wajib al-wujud (necessary existence)
concepts.definition: Avicennan proof of God as the being whose existence is necessary in itself.

concepts.name: Wahdat al-wujud (oneness of being)
concepts.definition: Sufi metaphysics asserting that all existence is one reality manifesting God.

concepts.name: Wahdat al-shuhud (oneness of witnessing)
concepts.definition: Sirhindi's alternative holding that perceived oneness is experiential, not ontological.

concepts.name: Hulul (indwelling)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that the divine inheres in a created being, condemned by mainstream theologians.

concepts.name: Ittihad (mystical union)
concepts.definition: Claim of unification between human and divine, contested by orthodox kalam.

concepts.name: Fana' (annihilation in God)
concepts.definition: Sufi state in which the self is extinguished in divine awareness.

concepts.name: Baqa' (subsistence in God)
concepts.definition: The post-annihilation state of subsisting through God after fana.

concepts.name: Al-insan al-kamil (the perfect human)
concepts.definition: Sufi metaphysical archetype embodying the fullness of divine attributes.

concepts.name: Al-haqiqa al-muhammadiyya (Muhammadan reality)
concepts.definition: The pre-eternal cosmic principle identified with the Prophet's inner reality.

concepts.name: Nur Muhammadi (Muhammadan light)
concepts.definition: Doctrine of a pre-creational divine light from which the Prophet and all things derive.

concepts.name: Al-a'yan al-thabita (immutable entities)
concepts.definition: Ibn Arabi's doctrine of fixed archetypes in divine knowledge prior to existentiation.

concepts.name: Tajalli (divine self-disclosure)
concepts.definition: God's manifestation of His attributes through creation and to mystics.

concepts.name: Khalq jadid (perpetual recreation)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that God continually recreates the universe at every instant.

concepts.name: Divine names cosmology
concepts.definition: Theological framework deriving creation and ethics from God's ninety-nine names.

concepts.name: Taklif (moral obligation)
concepts.definition: The grounds and limits of God imposing duties on rational creatures.

concepts.name: Ma'rifa (gnosis of God)
concepts.definition: Whether knowledge of God is obligatory by reason or only by revelation.

concepts.name: Taqlid in creed
concepts.definition: Whether ordinary believers may follow authority in matters of belief or must reason independently.

concepts.name: 'Aql wa naql (reason and revelation)
concepts.definition: How rational proofs and revealed texts relate when they appear to conflict.

concepts.name: Qanun al-ta'wil (rule of interpretation)
concepts.definition: Razi's rule prioritizing reason over apparent scripture in case of conflict.

concepts.name: Jiha (divine direction)
concepts.definition: Whether God can be said to occupy a direction such as 'above'.

concepts.name: Istiwa' (divine settling on the throne)
concepts.definition: How to understand the Qur'anic statement that God settled on the throne.

concepts.name: Definition of iman
concepts.definition: Whether faith is assent, speech and action, or includes increase and decrease.

concepts.name: Ziyadat al-iman (increase of faith)
concepts.definition: Whether faith fluctuates with works or remains constant.

concepts.name: Sam'iyyat (revealed-only matters)
concepts.definition: Eschatological and unseen doctrines knowable only through revelation, not reason.

concepts.name: Sifat al-fi'l (attributes of action)
concepts.definition: Whether divine acts like creating and providing are eternal attributes or temporal.

concepts.name: Takwin (divine bringing-into-being)
concepts.definition: Maturidi doctrine that 'creating' is an eternal attribute distinct from power.

concepts.name: 'Isma of prophets
concepts.definition: The scope of prophetic protection from sin before and after their mission.

concepts.name: Khilafa (caliphate as theological office)
concepts.definition: Whether legitimate succession to the Prophet is a creedal necessity.

concepts.name: Wajib al-wujud (necessary existence)
concepts.definition: Avicenna's proof of God as the being whose existence is necessary in itself versus contingent beings.

concepts.name: Mumkin al-wujud (contingent existence)
concepts.definition: Beings whose existence is possible and require an external cause to exist.

concepts.name: Distinction of essence and existence
concepts.definition: Whether existence is a real addition to essence or merely conceptual.

concepts.name: Asalat al-wujud (primacy of existence)
concepts.definition: Mulla Sadra's doctrine that existence is real and essences are mental abstractions.

concepts.name: Asalat al-mahiyya (primacy of essence)
concepts.definition: Suhrawardi's view that essences are real and existence is a mental concept.

concepts.name: Tashkik al-wujud (gradation of being)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that existence is a single reality admitting degrees of intensity.

concepts.name: Harakat jawhariyya (substantial motion)
concepts.definition: Mulla Sadra's doctrine that substances themselves undergo continuous change.

concepts.name: Ittihad al-'aqil wa'l-ma'qul (unity of intellect and intelligible)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that the knowing intellect becomes identical with what it knows.

concepts.name: Aql fa'al (active intellect)
concepts.definition: Cosmic intellect that bestows forms on matter and actualizes human knowledge.

concepts.name: Emanation of ten intellects
concepts.definition: Cosmological scheme where God produces a hierarchy of intellects governing celestial spheres.

concepts.name: Fayd (emanation)
concepts.definition: Necessary overflow of being from the One as the mechanism of creation.

concepts.name: Huduth dahri (atemporal origination)
concepts.definition: Mir Damad's doctrine of an origination outside time but not in eternity.

concepts.name: Critique of philosophers (tahafut)
concepts.definition: Ghazali's argument that philosophers contradict revelation on eternity, resurrection, and divine knowledge.

concepts.name: God's knowledge of particulars
concepts.definition: Whether God knows individual changing things or only universals.

concepts.name: Necessary causation
concepts.definition: Whether causes necessitate their effects or merely accompany them by divine custom.

concepts.name: Hayula and sura (matter and form)
concepts.definition: Aristotelian hylomorphic analysis of bodies as composites of prime matter and form.

concepts.name: Jawhar and 'arad (substance and accident)
concepts.definition: Categorial distinction between independently existing substances and their dependent properties.

concepts.name: Maqulat (the ten categories)
concepts.definition: Reception and reworking of Aristotle's ten categories in Arabic philosophy.

concepts.name: Kulli (universals)
concepts.definition: Whether universals exist in things, before things, or only in the mind.

concepts.name: Natural place and motion
concepts.definition: Aristotelian doctrine that elements seek their proper place in the cosmos.

concepts.name: Mayl (impressed inclination)
concepts.definition: Theory of impressed force in projectiles, anticipating impetus theory.

concepts.name: Khala' (the void)
concepts.definition: Whether empty space can exist within or beyond the cosmos.

concepts.name: Zaman (time)
concepts.definition: Whether time is the measure of motion, a real container, or an aspect of the soul.

concepts.name: Makan (place)
concepts.definition: Whether place is a containing surface, an interval, or a relation.

concepts.name: Actual and potential infinity
concepts.definition: Whether an actual infinite magnitude or set of causes can exist.

concepts.name: Nafs (the soul)
concepts.definition: Definition of the soul as substance, form, or perfection of the body.

concepts.name: Floating man argument
concepts.definition: Avicenna's thought experiment proving the soul's substantiality through self-awareness.

concepts.name: Stages of human intellect
concepts.definition: The progression from material to habitual to actual to acquired intellect.

concepts.name: Unity of the intellect
concepts.definition: Averroes' view that there is one shared material intellect for all humans.

concepts.name: Immortality of the rational soul
concepts.definition: Whether the individual soul survives bodily death.

concepts.name: Bodily resurrection in falsafa
concepts.definition: Whether philosophical principles permit literal bodily resurrection.

concepts.name: 'Alam al-mithal (imaginal world)
concepts.definition: Intermediate realm of suspended images between bodies and pure intellects.

concepts.name: Hads (intuition)
concepts.definition: Avicennan rapid intellectual grasp of middle terms without discursive reasoning.

concepts.name: Prophetic imagination
concepts.definition: The faculty by which prophets receive intelligibles as sensory images and symbols.

concepts.name: Hikmat al-ishraq (illuminationist wisdom)
concepts.definition: Suhrawardi's metaphysics of light as the basis of all reality and knowledge.

concepts.name: Ilm huduri (knowledge by presence)
concepts.definition: Direct, non-representational knowledge by which the soul knows itself.

concepts.name: Ilm husuli (acquired knowledge)
concepts.definition: Knowledge mediated by mental forms or representations of external things.

concepts.name: Burhan (demonstration)
concepts.definition: Aristotelian demonstrative syllogism yielding certain knowledge from necessary premises.

concepts.name: Qiyas (logical syllogism)
concepts.definition: The categorical syllogism as the central tool of philosophical reasoning.

concepts.name: Hypothetical and disjunctive syllogism
concepts.definition: Avicenna's expansion of logic to conditional and disjunctive propositions beyond Aristotle.

concepts.name: Modal logic in falsafa
concepts.definition: Analysis of necessary, possible, and impossible propositions and their inferences.

concepts.name: Five arts of logic
concepts.definition: Classification of arguments into demonstration, dialectic, rhetoric, poetics, and sophistry.

concepts.name: Five predicables
concepts.definition: Genus, species, difference, property, and accident as the basis of definition and division.

concepts.name: Tasawwur and tasdiq (conception and assent)
concepts.definition: Distinction between forming a concept and judging its truth as the two acts of knowing.

concepts.name: Privation theory of evil
concepts.definition: Doctrine that evil has no positive existence but is the absence of good.

concepts.name: Inaya (divine providence)
concepts.definition: How God's foreknowledge and goodness order the cosmos toward the best outcome.

concepts.name: Sa'ada (ultimate happiness)
concepts.definition: The intellectual conjunction with the active intellect as humanity's final perfection.

concepts.name: Al-madina al-fadila (virtuous city)
concepts.definition: Farabi's political philosophy of a city ruled by a philosopher-prophet for human perfection.

concepts.name: Governance of the solitary
concepts.definition: Ibn Bajja's account of the philosopher's life in an imperfect society.

concepts.name: Hayy ibn Yaqzan thought experiment
concepts.definition: Whether an isolated human can attain truth and God by unaided reason.

concepts.name: Harmony of philosophy and revelation
concepts.definition: Whether demonstrative philosophy and revealed religion can yield the same truth.

concepts.name: Double truth (attributed)
concepts.definition: Polemical claim that philosophy and religion may hold contradictory truths simultaneously.

concepts.name: Numerical cosmology of the Brethren
concepts.definition: Pythagorean-Neoplatonic cosmology grounding reality in number and harmony.

concepts.name: Isma'ili philosophical ta'wil
concepts.definition: Esoteric interpretation linking scripture to a Neoplatonic cosmic hierarchy.

concepts.name: Ibda' (ex nihilo origination)
concepts.definition: Isma'ili doctrine that God originates the first intellect without instrument or matter.

concepts.name: Aql awwal (first intellect)
concepts.definition: The first emanated being from which all other existents proceed.

concepts.name: Tanasukh (transmigration)
concepts.definition: Whether souls migrate between bodies after death, debated and largely rejected.

concepts.name: Razi's five eternals
concepts.definition: Abu Bakr al-Razi's doctrine of God, soul, matter, time, and space as co-eternal principles.

concepts.name: Spiritual medicine of the soul
concepts.definition: Philosophical therapy of the passions modeled on bodily medicine.

concepts.name: Tahdhib al-akhlaq (refinement of character)
concepts.definition: Philosophical ethics of acquiring virtues through habituation and reason.

concepts.name: Doctrine of the mean
concepts.definition: Aristotelian virtue as the rational mean between extremes of excess and deficiency.

concepts.name: Practical intellect
concepts.definition: The rational faculty governing action as distinct from theoretical knowledge.

concepts.name: Siyasa madaniyya (political science)
concepts.definition: Philosophical inquiry into the best regime and the lawgiver's role.

concepts.name: Celestial spheres causation
concepts.definition: How motions of celestial bodies mediate God's action on the sublunar world.

concepts.name: Intermediate causes
concepts.definition: Hierarchy of secondary causes through which the First Cause acts.

concepts.name: Divine simplicity
concepts.definition: God as absolutely simple, with no composition of parts, attributes, or essence and existence.

concepts.name: Basit al-haqiqa (the simple reality)
concepts.definition: Sadrian principle that what is simple in essence contains all perfections.

concepts.name: I'tibariyyat (mental constructs)
concepts.definition: Concepts with no extramental referent yet indispensable to thought, like essence or causality.

concepts.name: Critique of Aristotelian logic
concepts.definition: Internal Islamic critiques of definition, syllogism, and the categories.

concepts.name: Usul al-fiqh (legal theory)
concepts.definition: The discipline establishing the sources, methods, and interpretive principles of Islamic law.

concepts.name: Ijtihad (independent legal reasoning)
concepts.definition: The qualified jurist's exertion to derive rulings from the sources of law.

concepts.name: Taqlid (following authority)
concepts.definition: The lay or scholar's adherence to a qualified jurist without independent derivation.

concepts.name: Closing of the gate of ijtihad
concepts.definition: Disputed thesis that independent legal reasoning ceased after the formative period.

concepts.name: Qiyas (analogical reasoning)
concepts.definition: Extending a ruling from a textual case to a new case sharing the same effective cause.

concepts.name: 'Illa (effective cause)
concepts.definition: The legally operative attribute that triggers a ruling and grounds analogy.

concepts.name: Takhrij, tanqih, tahqiq al-manat
concepts.definition: The three techniques for identifying, refining, and verifying the cause of a ruling.

concepts.name: Ijma' (scholarly consensus)
concepts.definition: The binding agreement of qualified jurists of a generation on a legal ruling.

concepts.name: Ijma' sukuti (tacit consensus)
concepts.definition: Whether a ruling held by some jurists with the silence of others counts as consensus.

concepts.name: Ijma' of the Ahl al-Bayt
concepts.definition: Shia doctrine that consensus is authoritative only when it includes an infallible imam.

concepts.name: Khabar al-wahid (solitary report)
concepts.definition: Whether a single-chain hadith yields certain or only probable legal knowledge.

concepts.name: Mutawatir reports
concepts.definition: Mass-transmitted reports yielding certainty and binding legal authority.

concepts.name: Amal ahl al-Madina (practice of Medina)
concepts.definition: Maliki doctrine treating the living practice of Medina as a normative legal source.

concepts.name: Qawl al-sahabi (companion's opinion)
concepts.definition: Whether the legal opinion of a Prophetic companion is binding on later jurists.

concepts.name: Shar' man qablana (laws of prior prophets)
concepts.definition: Whether revealed laws of earlier prophets remain binding for Muslims.

concepts.name: Istihsan (juristic preference)
concepts.definition: Setting aside strict analogy for a stronger consideration of equity or scripture.

concepts.name: Istislah / maslaha mursala (unattested public interest)
concepts.definition: Basing rulings on public benefit not directly addressed by a text.

concepts.name: Maqasid al-shari'a (higher objectives of law)
concepts.definition: The protection of religion, life, intellect, lineage, and property as law's purposes.

concepts.name: Daruriyyat, hajiyyat, tahsiniyyat
concepts.definition: Tripartite ranking of legal interests as necessities, needs, and refinements.

concepts.name: Sadd al-dhara'i' (blocking the means)
concepts.definition: Prohibiting otherwise lawful acts that predictably lead to forbidden outcomes.

concepts.name: Fath al-dhara'i' (opening the means)
concepts.definition: Permitting acts that lead to recognized goods even if otherwise restricted.

concepts.name: 'Urf (custom)
concepts.definition: Recognized social custom as a basis for or qualifier of legal rulings.

concepts.name: Istishab (presumption of continuity)
concepts.definition: Presuming a prior legal state to continue absent evidence of change.

concepts.name: Bara'a asliyya (original non-liability)
concepts.definition: Default principle that persons are free of obligation until proven otherwise.

concepts.name: Ibaha asliyya (presumption of permissibility)
concepts.definition: Default that things are permissible unless a text prohibits them.

concepts.name: Amm and khass (general and particular)
concepts.definition: How general scriptural expressions interact with particular qualifying texts.

concepts.name: Mutlaq and muqayyad (absolute and qualified)
concepts.definition: How an unqualified text is read in light of a related qualified one.

concepts.name: Mujmal and mubayyan (unclear and clarified)
concepts.definition: Distinguishing texts requiring clarification from those that clarify them.

concepts.name: Nass and zahir (explicit and apparent)
concepts.definition: Hierarchy of textual clarity from unambiguous statements to apparent meanings.

concepts.name: Haqiqa and majaz (literal and figurative)
concepts.definition: Whether scripture should be taken literally or admits figurative interpretation.

concepts.name: Amr and nahy (command and prohibition)
concepts.definition: Whether scriptural commands imply obligation and prohibitions imply invalidity.

concepts.name: Naskh (abrogation)
concepts.definition: The doctrine that later revealed rulings can supersede earlier ones.

concepts.name: Takhsis (specification)
concepts.definition: Restricting a general scriptural text by another evidence.

concepts.name: Ta'arud and tarjih (conflict and weighing)
concepts.definition: Methods for resolving and weighting apparently conflicting scriptural evidences.

concepts.name: Al-hukm al-shar'i (legal ruling)
concepts.definition: The five-fold classification of acts as obligatory, recommended, permitted, disliked, or forbidden.

concepts.name: Fard and wajib distinction
concepts.definition: Hanafi distinction between obligations grounded in certain versus probable evidence.

concepts.name: Fard kifaya (collective obligation)
concepts.definition: Duties whose performance by some Muslims relieves the obligation from the rest.

concepts.name: Rukhsa and 'azima (concession and resolve)
concepts.definition: Distinction between strict legal rulings and concessions granted under hardship.

concepts.name: Darura (necessity)
concepts.definition: The principle that necessity makes the otherwise forbidden permissible within limits.

concepts.name: Mashaqqa tajlib al-taysir (hardship brings ease)
concepts.definition: Maxim that legal hardship triggers concessions and lighter rulings.

concepts.name: Qawa'id fiqhiyya (legal maxims)
concepts.definition: Concise principles synthesizing rulings across diverse cases.

concepts.name: Furuq (legal distinctions)
concepts.definition: Genre identifying subtle differences between superficially similar legal cases.

concepts.name: Ikhtilaf (juristic disagreement)
concepts.definition: The discipline of cataloging and analyzing legitimate differences between jurists.

concepts.name: Takhayyur (selecting across schools)
concepts.definition: Modern method of choosing rulings from different schools to address new needs.

concepts.name: Talfiq (combining school rulings)
concepts.definition: Constructing a single act from rulings of more than one school, traditionally restricted.

concepts.name: Fatwa (juristic responsum)
concepts.definition: A non-binding scholarly legal opinion issued in response to a question.

concepts.name: Qada' (judgeship)
concepts.definition: The institution and ethics of judicial office and adjudication.

concepts.name: Shahada (testimony)
concepts.definition: Rules governing witness eligibility, number, and evidentiary weight.

concepts.name: Yamin (judicial oath)
concepts.definition: The role of oaths in resolving disputes when evidence is insufficient.

concepts.name: Bayyina (proof)
concepts.definition: The standards of probative evidence required to establish a legal claim.

concepts.name: Hudud (fixed penalties)
concepts.definition: Scripturally fixed punishments for theft, adultery, defamation, intoxication, and apostasy.

concepts.name: Qisas (retaliation)
concepts.definition: Equivalent retribution for homicide and bodily injury, subject to victim's family.

concepts.name: Diya (blood money)
concepts.definition: Compensatory payment for homicide or injury in lieu of or alongside retaliation.

concepts.name: Ta'zir (discretionary punishment)
concepts.definition: Judge-determined penalties for offenses lacking a fixed scriptural sanction.

concepts.name: Siyasa shar'iyya (governance within sharia)
concepts.definition: The ruler's discretionary authority to legislate and adjudicate beyond fixed law.

concepts.name: Hisba (market and moral oversight)
concepts.definition: The office regulating commerce, weights, and public morality.

concepts.name: Riba (usury and interest)
concepts.definition: The prohibition of unjust increase in loans and exchange of like commodities.

concepts.name: Gharar (excessive uncertainty)
concepts.definition: Prohibition of contracts whose object or outcome is unduly uncertain.

concepts.name: Hiyal (legal stratagems)
concepts.definition: Formally permissible devices to achieve outcomes otherwise restricted by law.

concepts.name: Waqf (charitable endowment)
concepts.definition: The legal institution of irrevocable dedication of property for pious or family use.

concepts.name: Zakat (obligatory almsgiving)
concepts.definition: Legal rules governing the obligatory annual wealth tax and its distribution.

concepts.name: Khums (one-fifth tax)
concepts.definition: Shia obligation to pay one-fifth of annual surplus to the imam or his deputies.

concepts.name: Jizya (poll tax on non-Muslims)
concepts.definition: The protection tax levied on non-Muslim subjects under Islamic rule.

concepts.name: Dhimma (protection contract)
concepts.definition: The legal status of non-Muslims as protected residents with defined rights and duties.

concepts.name: Siyar (law of nations and warfare)
concepts.definition: Rules governing relations between Muslim polities and others, including conduct of war.

concepts.name: Jihad (legal doctrine of armed struggle)
concepts.definition: Legal classification, conditions, and limits of religiously sanctioned warfare.

concepts.name: Aman (safe-conduct)
concepts.definition: Grant of legal protection allowing non-Muslims temporary entry to Muslim territory.

concepts.name: Nikah (marriage contract)
concepts.definition: The legal contract creating marital rights, including conditions, witnesses, and dower.

concepts.name: Mahr (dower)
concepts.definition: The obligatory bridal gift from husband to wife as a pillar of marriage.

concepts.name: Talaq (repudiation)
concepts.definition: The husband's unilateral dissolution of marriage and its procedural constraints.

concepts.name: Khul' (wife-initiated divorce)
concepts.definition: Dissolution of marriage at the wife's initiative through compensation to the husband.

concepts.name: Mut'a (temporary marriage)
concepts.definition: Time-limited marriage permitted in Twelver Shia law and rejected by Sunnis.

concepts.name: Fara'id (inheritance shares)
concepts.definition: The fixed Quranic shares and rules of intestate succession.

concepts.name: 'Awl and radd (proportional adjustment)
concepts.definition: Techniques for proportional reduction or restoration when inheritance shares mismatch the estate.

concepts.name: Tasawwuf (the discipline of Sufism)
concepts.definition: The science of purifying the heart and traversing the path to God.

concepts.name: Ihsan (spiritual excellence)
concepts.definition: Worshipping God as if seeing Him, the prophetic root of mystical practice.

concepts.name: Zuhd (renunciation)
concepts.definition: Detachment from worldly attachments as the foundation of the spiritual path.

concepts.name: Wara' (scrupulousness)
concepts.definition: Avoiding the doubtful in food, speech, and conduct beyond legal requirement.

concepts.name: Tawba (repentance)
concepts.definition: The first station of the path, turning the heart from sin back to God.

concepts.name: Sabr (patience)
concepts.definition: Steadfast endurance under hardship as a station on the spiritual path.

concepts.name: Shukr (gratitude)
concepts.definition: Recognition that every blessing originates from God as a station of the heart.

concepts.name: Khawf and raja' (fear and hope)
concepts.definition: The balanced inner states of fearing God's punishment and hoping for His mercy.

concepts.name: Tawakkul (reliance on God)
concepts.definition: Absolute trust in God's provision while engaging or abandoning means.

concepts.name: Rida (contentment with God's decree)
concepts.definition: Inward acceptance of all God ordains, sweet or bitter, without complaint.

concepts.name: Mahabba (divine love)
concepts.definition: Love of God as the engine of the path, debated as a station and a state.

concepts.name: 'Ishq (passionate love)
concepts.definition: Intense, intoxicating love for God beyond rational mahabba.

concepts.name: Shawq (longing)
concepts.definition: The ache of yearning for divine encounter as a state of the lover.

concepts.name: Uns (intimacy with God)
concepts.definition: The state of intimate familiarity replacing fear at advanced stages.

concepts.name: Qabd and bast (contraction and expansion)
concepts.definition: Alternating divine states of constriction and openness in the wayfarer's heart.

concepts.name: Hayba and uns (awe and intimacy)
concepts.definition: The paired states of overwhelming awe before God and intimate nearness.

concepts.name: Sukr and sahw (intoxication and sobriety)
concepts.definition: Whether spiritual ecstasy or lucid sobriety marks the higher mystical station.

concepts.name: Shath (ecstatic utterance)
concepts.definition: Paradoxical or theopathic speech uttered in mystical intoxication.

concepts.name: Wahdat al-wujud (oneness of being)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that all existence is one reality manifesting the single divine being.

concepts.name: Five divine presences
concepts.definition: Hierarchical levels of reality from absolute mystery to the human microcosm.

concepts.name: Al-insan al-kamil (the perfect human)
concepts.definition: The cosmic archetype embodying the totality of divine names and attributes.

concepts.name: Lata'if (subtle centers)
concepts.definition: Subtle spiritual organs of the heart cultivated through invocation and discipline.

concepts.name: Qalb (the spiritual heart)
concepts.definition: The locus of gnosis, distinct from the physical organ, central to mystical psychology.

concepts.name: Nafs (stages of the lower self)
concepts.definition: The sevenfold ascent from the commanding self to the soul at peace with God.

concepts.name: Ruh (the spirit)
concepts.definition: The divine breath in the human, debated as eternal, created, or intermediate.

concepts.name: Sirr (the secret)
concepts.definition: The innermost subtle center where God's mystery is directly known.

concepts.name: Khatir (passing thought)
concepts.definition: Discernment of fleeting suggestions from the soul, angel, devil, or God.

concepts.name: Muhasaba (self-examination)
concepts.definition: Daily reckoning of one's intentions and acts as a discipline of the heart.

concepts.name: Muraqaba (vigilant awareness)
concepts.definition: Sustained mindful attention to God's presence as a meditative practice.

concepts.name: Dhikr (invocation of God)
concepts.definition: Ritualized remembrance of God by formula, name, or breath as the central Sufi practice.

concepts.name: Dhikr jali and khafi (vocal and silent)
concepts.definition: Disputed practice of audible group invocation versus silent inward remembrance.

concepts.name: Sama' (spiritual audition)
concepts.definition: The use of poetry, song, and music to induce mystical states, contested by jurists.

concepts.name: Hadra (collective remembrance gathering)
concepts.definition: The Sufi assembly of group dhikr, often with movement and chant.

concepts.name: Khalwa (spiritual retreat)
concepts.definition: Solitary seclusion devoted to prayer, fasting, and dhikr under a master's direction.

concepts.name: Arba'in (forty-day retreat)
concepts.definition: The classical forty-day seclusion modeled on Moses and the Prophet.

concepts.name: Riyada (spiritual training)
concepts.definition: Systematic ascetic exercises that discipline the lower self.

concepts.name: Mujahada (inner struggle)
concepts.definition: The greater jihad against the lower self as the engine of spiritual transformation.

concepts.name: Tariqa (the path)
concepts.definition: The structured spiritual method linking shari'a outwardly to haqiqa inwardly.

concepts.name: Shari'a, tariqa, haqiqa
concepts.definition: The threefold framework of outward law, inward path, and ultimate reality.

concepts.name: Maqamat and ahwal (stations and states)
concepts.definition: Distinction between earned spiritual stations and gifted transient states.

concepts.name: Suhba (spiritual companionship)
concepts.definition: The transformative discipleship of constant companionship with a master.

concepts.name: Bay'a (initiatic pact)
concepts.definition: The oath of allegiance binding the disciple to a shaykh and his lineage.

concepts.name: Silsila (chain of transmission)
concepts.definition: The unbroken lineage of masters transmitting spiritual authority back to the Prophet.

concepts.name: Ijaza (initiatic license)
concepts.definition: Authorization granted by a master to transmit invocations or guide disciples.

concepts.name: Khirqa (mantle of initiation)
concepts.definition: The patched cloak conferred by a shaykh symbolizing entry into the path.

concepts.name: Futuwwa (spiritual chivalry)
concepts.definition: The mystical ethics of generosity, self-sacrifice, and brotherhood.

concepts.name: Adab (spiritual courtesy)
concepts.definition: The refined inward and outward etiquette of the wayfarer with God and people.

concepts.name: Himma (spiritual aspiration)
concepts.definition: The concentrated will of the heart that effects change in the soul and the world.

concepts.name: Kashf (unveiling)
concepts.definition: Direct intuitive disclosure of unseen realities to the purified heart.

concepts.name: Ilham (divine inspiration)
concepts.definition: Non-prophetic inspiration cast into the heart, contested as a source of knowledge.

concepts.name: Firasa (spiritual physiognomy)
concepts.definition: Insight into hidden states through illuminated discernment of outward signs.

concepts.name: Karamat (saintly miracles)
concepts.definition: Extraordinary acts granted to friends of God, distinguished from prophetic miracles.

concepts.name: Wilaya (sainthood)
concepts.definition: The state of being a friend of God, with debated relation to prophethood.

concepts.name: Khatm al-awliya' (seal of the saints)
concepts.definition: The eschatological saint who closes the cycle of sainthood as Muhammad closed prophecy.

concepts.name: Qutb (the axial saint)
concepts.definition: The pole around whom the spiritual hierarchy of the age revolves.

concepts.name: Abdal (the substitutes)
concepts.definition: Hidden saints who sustain the cosmic order and replace one another upon death.

concepts.name: Rijal al-ghayb (men of the unseen)
concepts.definition: The hierarchy of unseen saints administering the spiritual government of the world.

concepts.name: Khidr as initiator
concepts.definition: The immortal guide who initiates uwaysi seekers without a living master.

concepts.name: Uwaysi transmission
concepts.definition: Initiation received from a deceased or absent master through spiritual contact.

concepts.name: Tawajjuh (spiritual focusing)
concepts.definition: The directed concentration by which a master transmits grace to a disciple.

concepts.name: Rabita (binding to the shaykh)
concepts.definition: Visualizing the master as a channel of grace, contested as innovation.

concepts.name: Tawassul (intercessory mediation)
concepts.definition: Seeking nearness to God through prophets and saints, contested by reformists.

concepts.name: Ziyara (visitation of tombs)
concepts.definition: Pilgrimage to graves of prophets and saints for blessing, debated in legitimacy.

concepts.name: Baraka (transmissible blessing)
concepts.definition: Sanctifying grace flowing through saints, places, objects, and lineages.

concepts.name: Mi'raj (mystical ascent)
concepts.definition: The Prophet's night ascent reread as a paradigm for the soul's journey to God.

concepts.name: Sayr wa suluk (wayfaring)
concepts.definition: The technical map of the soul's journey through stations toward God.

concepts.name: Sayr fi'llah and ila'llah (journey to and in God)
concepts.definition: Distinction between approaching God and the endless journey within Him.

concepts.name: Arcs of descent and ascent
concepts.definition: The cosmic cycle of being descending from God and returning to Him through the human.

concepts.name: 'Alam al-mithal (imaginal world)
concepts.definition: Intermediate realm of subtle forms where visions and dreams are objectively real.

concepts.name: Khayal (creative imagination)
concepts.definition: The faculty by which God and the mystic give form to spiritual realities.

concepts.name: Ru'ya sadiqa (true dreams)
concepts.definition: Veridical dreams as a recognized channel of unseen knowledge.

concepts.name: Tafsir ishari (allusive Qur'anic exegesis)
concepts.definition: Mystical Qur'an interpretation drawing inner meanings from outward text.

concepts.name: Zahir and batin (outer and inner)
concepts.definition: The doctrine that scripture and reality have manifest and hidden dimensions.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-huruf (science of letters)
concepts.definition: Esoteric cosmology deriving meaning and power from Arabic letters and names.

concepts.name: Jafr (esoteric divination)
concepts.definition: Lettrist technique of foretelling and decoding hidden realities attributed to Ali and Ja'far al-Sadiq.

concepts.name: Abjad numerology
concepts.definition: Assigning numerical values to letters to uncover hidden meanings in scripture.

concepts.name: 'Irfan (Shia gnosis)
concepts.definition: Shia mystical philosophy synthesizing Akbari metaphysics with Twelver theology.

concepts.name: Walaya (Shia spiritual authority)
concepts.definition: The esoteric authority of Ali and the imams as the inner dimension of prophecy.

concepts.name: Samt (mystical silence)
concepts.definition: Disciplined silence of tongue and heart as a station of the wayfarer.

concepts.name: Ju' (spiritual hunger)
concepts.definition: Sustained fasting and reduction of food as a key ascetic discipline.

concepts.name: Sahar (night vigil)
concepts.definition: Standing in prayer and remembrance through the night as a core Sufi discipline.

concepts.name: Faqr (spiritual poverty)
concepts.definition: Inner emptiness before God, the badge of the Sufi beyond mere material poverty.

concepts.name: Ikhlas (sincerity)
concepts.definition: Purifying intention so that acts are done for God alone, free of self-display.

concepts.name: Riya' (spiritual ostentation)
concepts.definition: The hidden disease of performing worship for human regard, the chief target of self-scrutiny.

concepts.name: Imama (Sunni theory of leadership)
concepts.definition: The legal and theological doctrine of appointing and obeying a single legitimate ruler.

concepts.name: Imama (Shia imamate)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that political and spiritual authority belongs to divinely designated imams from Ali's line.

concepts.name: Bay'a (oath of allegiance)
concepts.definition: The contractual pledge binding subjects and elites to a new ruler.

concepts.name: Shura (consultation)
concepts.definition: The Quranic duty of consultative decision-making in selecting and advising rulers.

concepts.name: Ahl al-hall wa'l-'aqd (people who loose and bind)
concepts.definition: The qualified notables whose consensus legitimates the ruler.

concepts.name: Nass (designation of successor)
concepts.definition: Explicit appointment of a successor, central to Shia legitimacy claims.

concepts.name: Qurayshi lineage requirement
concepts.definition: Classical stipulation that the caliph must descend from Quraysh, later contested.

concepts.name: Khariji elective imamate
concepts.definition: The view that any qualified Muslim, regardless of lineage, may be elected imam.

concepts.name: Zaydi qualified imamate
concepts.definition: Zaydi doctrine that the imam must be a learned Fatimid who rises in arms against injustice.

concepts.name: Isma'ili living imamate
concepts.definition: Doctrine of a continuously present, hereditary imam possessing esoteric authority.

concepts.name: Ghayba (occultation and political authority)
concepts.definition: The question of legitimate governance during the Twelfth Imam's hiddenness.

concepts.name: Hisba (public moral oversight)
concepts.definition: The office commanding right and forbidding wrong in markets and public life.

concepts.name: Al-madina al-fadila (virtuous city)
concepts.definition: Farabi's philosophical ideal of a polity ruled by a philosopher-prophet for human perfection.

concepts.name: Ra'is al-madina (philosopher-ruler)
concepts.definition: The figure combining wisdom, revelation, and practical governance at the head of the city.

concepts.name: Adab al-muluk (mirrors for princes)
concepts.definition: The genre of practical counsel on just rulership, statecraft, and royal ethics.

concepts.name: Circle of justice
concepts.definition: The axiom that kingship requires army, army requires wealth, wealth requires subjects, subjects require justice.

concepts.name: 'Adl (political justice)
concepts.definition: Justice as the primary duty and legitimating function of the ruler.

concepts.name: Zulm (tyranny)
concepts.definition: Unjust rule as the paradigmatic failure of political legitimacy.

concepts.name: Obedience to the unjust ruler
concepts.definition: Whether Muslims must obey a sinful or tyrannical ruler to preserve public order.

concepts.name: Khuruj (armed rebellion)
concepts.definition: The legitimacy of rising in arms against a ruler judged unjust or unbelieving.

concepts.name: Fitna (civil strife)
concepts.definition: The theological-political category of communal discord to be avoided at nearly any cost.

concepts.name: Commanding right and forbidding wrong (political)
concepts.definition: The duty to correct rulers and public wrongs, ranging from counsel to armed action.

concepts.name: Dar al-Islam and dar al-harb
concepts.definition: Legal division of the world into the abode of Islam and the abode of war.

concepts.name: Dar al-'ahd / dar al-sulh (abode of treaty)
concepts.definition: Intermediate legal zone of non-Muslim polities bound to Muslims by peace treaty.

concepts.name: Dhimma (protected non-Muslim subjects)
concepts.definition: The contract defining rights, duties, and restrictions of non-Muslims under Muslim rule.

concepts.name: Jihad (political-military doctrine)
concepts.definition: The legal theory of warfare authorized and regulated by legitimate Muslim authority.

concepts.name: Bughat (legal rebels)
concepts.definition: The legal category of Muslim rebels who may be fought but retain specific protections.

concepts.name: 'Asabiyya (group solidarity)
concepts.definition: Ibn Khaldun's doctrine of tribal cohesion as the engine of dynastic rise and decline.
concepts.notes: Foundational concept of historical sociology of politics.

concepts.name: Dawla (dynastic cycle)
concepts.definition: The theory that polities pass through regular stages of rise, luxury, and collapse.

concepts.name: Mulk (kingship) vs khilafa
concepts.definition: The distinction between religiously guided caliphate and mere coercive monarchy.

concepts.name: Sultana (delegated temporal authority)
concepts.definition: The legal recognition of sultans exercising real power under a symbolic caliph.

concepts.name: Taghallub (legitimation by seizure)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that effective conquest and control can legitimate an otherwise irregular ruler.

concepts.name: Nasiha (counsel to rulers)
concepts.definition: The scholar's duty to advise and correct rulers privately rather than revolt.

concepts.name: 'Ulama and state authority
concepts.definition: The evolving relationship between scholarly legal authority and ruling political power.

concepts.name: Modern Islamic state
concepts.definition: 20th-century project of reconstituting a polity grounded in Islamic law and identity.

concepts.name: Hakimiyya (divine sovereignty)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that legislative sovereignty belongs to God alone, foundational to modern Islamism.

concepts.name: Umma (global Muslim community)
concepts.definition: The transpolitical unity of Muslims as a single community across states and borders.

concepts.name: Tabi'iyyat (natural philosophy)
concepts.definition: The systematic study of the natural world within the Aristotelian-Avicennan tradition.

concepts.name: Experimental method (i'tibar)
concepts.definition: Systematic experiment and controlled observation as the test of physical theories.
concepts.notes: Ibn al-Haytham's i'tibar anticipates key features of modern experimental science.

concepts.name: Istiqra' (induction)
concepts.definition: Reasoning from particular observations to general scientific principles.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-manazir (science of optics)
concepts.definition: The study of vision, light, reflection, and refraction as a mathematical science.

concepts.name: Intromission theory of vision
concepts.definition: The doctrine that sight occurs when light from objects enters the eye.

concepts.name: Theory of the rainbow
concepts.definition: Explaining the rainbow through two refractions and an internal reflection in raindrops.

concepts.name: Law of refraction (Ibn Sahl)
concepts.definition: Geometrical rule relating angles of incidence and refraction at transparent interfaces.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-hay'a (theoretical astronomy)
concepts.definition: Mathematical modeling of celestial motions by spherical configurations.

concepts.name: Shukuk 'ala Batlamyus (doubts on Ptolemy)
concepts.definition: Physical and philosophical objections to Ptolemaic devices like the equant.

concepts.name: Tusi couple
concepts.definition: Geometric device producing linear motion from two circular motions, used to reform planetary models.

concepts.name: Urdi lemma
concepts.definition: Geometric theorem enabling non-Ptolemaic planetary models at Maragha.

concepts.name: Ibn al-Shatir's planetary model
concepts.definition: Non-equant lunar and planetary models mathematically equivalent to later Copernican constructions.

concepts.name: Possibility of earth's rotation
concepts.definition: Debate on whether observations require a stationary earth or permit its rotation.

concepts.name: Trepidation of the equinoxes
concepts.definition: Theory of an oscillatory motion superimposed on equinoctial precession.

concepts.name: Andalusi homocentric astronomy
concepts.definition: Attempt to restore Aristotelian concentric spheres against Ptolemaic eccentrics and epicycles.

concepts.name: Zij (astronomical tables)
concepts.definition: Handbooks of tables and parameters for computing positions of celestial bodies.

concepts.name: Qibla determination
concepts.definition: Mathematical methods for finding the direction of Mecca from any terrestrial point.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-miqat (timekeeping science)
concepts.definition: Astronomical determination of prayer times, new moons, and ritual calendars.

concepts.name: Astrolabe theory
concepts.definition: Geometry and use of the projection instrument for astronomy, timekeeping, and qibla.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-jabr wa'l-muqabala (algebra)
concepts.definition: Systematic solution of equations by restoration and balancing of terms.

concepts.name: Geometric solution of cubics
concepts.definition: Solving third-degree equations by intersecting conic sections.

concepts.name: Decimal fractions
concepts.definition: Representation of fractions in positional decimal notation for computation.

concepts.name: Combinatorial mathematics
concepts.definition: Counting arrangements, permutations, and combinations in arithmetic and linguistics.

concepts.name: Binomial expansion and Pascal's triangle
concepts.definition: Expansion of powers of a binomial through the arithmetic triangle.

concepts.name: Parallel postulate investigations
concepts.definition: Attempts to prove Euclid's fifth postulate, anticipating non-Euclidean geometry.

concepts.name: Spherical trigonometry
concepts.definition: Systematic treatment of sine, tangent, and spherical triangles for astronomy.

concepts.name: Law of sines
concepts.definition: Trigonometric relation generalizing sides and angles in plane and spherical triangles.

concepts.name: Mayl (impressed inclination)
concepts.definition: Theory of impressed force in projectiles anticipating impetus dynamics.

concepts.name: Specific gravity measurements
concepts.definition: Precise determination of densities of metals, gems, and liquids by hydrostatic methods.

concepts.name: Science of weights (hiyal and mizan)
concepts.definition: Mechanical theory of simple machines, balances, and equilibria.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-hiyal (ingenious devices)
concepts.definition: Design and theory of automata, clocks, and self-operating machines.

concepts.name: Tibb (Galenic-Islamic medicine)
concepts.definition: Integrated medical theory based on humors, temperaments, and causes of disease.

concepts.name: Four humors (akhlat)
concepts.definition: Doctrine that health arises from the balance of blood, phlegm, yellow and black bile.

concepts.name: Mizaj (temperament)
concepts.definition: The individual's specific humoral balance determining health, character, and treatment.

concepts.name: Pulmonary circulation
concepts.definition: Ibn al-Nafis's discovery that blood passes from right to left heart through the lungs.

concepts.name: Contagion ('adwa) debate
concepts.definition: Dispute over whether diseases spread by natural contagion or only by divine will.
concepts.notes: Prominent during the Black Death in al-Andalus.

concepts.name: Differential diagnosis of smallpox and measles
concepts.definition: Clinical distinction between two eruptive fevers pioneered by al-Razi.

concepts.name: Surgical practice
concepts.definition: Systematic treatise tradition of surgical instruments, procedures, and cauterization.

concepts.name: Bimaristan (teaching hospital)
concepts.definition: The institution integrating patient care, specialized wards, and medical training.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-adwiya (materia medica)
concepts.definition: Systematic classification of simple and compound drugs with their properties.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-kuhl (ophthalmology)
concepts.definition: Systematic treatise tradition on eye anatomy, diseases, and surgical treatments.

concepts.name: Kimiya (alchemy)
concepts.definition: Theory and practice of transmutation grounded in sulfur-mercury and elixir doctrines.

concepts.name: Sulfur-mercury theory
concepts.definition: Doctrine that all metals are composed of varying proportions of sulfur and mercury.

concepts.name: Critique of alchemical transmutation
concepts.definition: Philosophical argument that species-change of metals is impossible in principle.

concepts.name: Masalik wa mamalik (human geography)
concepts.definition: Genre mapping routes, regions, cities, and peoples of the known world.

concepts.name: Mathematical geography
concepts.definition: Determination of latitudes, longitudes, and coordinates for cities and landmarks.

concepts.name: Measurement of earth's circumference
concepts.definition: Geodetic techniques for computing the size of the earth from celestial and terrestrial observations.

concepts.name: Seven climes (aqalim)
concepts.definition: Ancient division of the inhabited world into seven latitudinal bands shaping peoples.

concepts.name: Mineralogy and gemology
concepts.definition: Classification and testing of minerals, stones, and gems and their properties.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-nabat (botany)
concepts.definition: Systematic description and classification of plants and their medicinal uses.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-hayawan (zoology)
concepts.definition: Descriptive and behavioral study of animals, often integrating Aristotle and Arabic observation.

concepts.name: Filaha (agronomy)
concepts.definition: Scientific agriculture covering soils, irrigation, crops, and grafting.

concepts.name: Cartographic representation
concepts.definition: Theory and technique of producing maps of regions and the world.

concepts.name: Celestial sphere cosmology (aflak)
concepts.definition: Model of concentric spheres carrying sun, moon, planets, and fixed stars.

concepts.name: Ahkam al-nujum (judicial astrology)
concepts.definition: Predictive science of celestial influences on persons, states, and events.

concepts.name: Critique of astrology
concepts.definition: Scientific and theological rejection of predictive astrology as unsound or impious.

concepts.name: Classification of the sciences
concepts.definition: Systematic ordering and definition of the religious and rational sciences.

concepts.name: Mathematization of physics
concepts.definition: Programmatic insistence that optical and mechanical problems admit geometrical proof.

concepts.name: Naturalism (tab') vs occasionalism
concepts.definition: Debate over whether natural causes act by intrinsic powers or only by divine custom.

concepts.name: Marsad (observatory institution)
concepts.definition: Dedicated institution for systematic long-term astronomical observation and instrument-making.

concepts.name: Islam and modern science (modern debate)
concepts.definition: Modern reformist argument that Islam is compatible with and anticipated modern science.

concepts.name: Nahw (Arabic grammar / syntax)
concepts.definition: The systematic study of Arabic sentence structure, governance, and inflection.

concepts.name: Sarf (morphology)
concepts.definition: The science of word formation, derivation, and patterns of Arabic roots.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-lugha (lexicography)
concepts.definition: The collection, definition, and organization of the Arabic lexicon.

concepts.name: 'Amil (syntactic governance)
concepts.definition: The doctrine that certain words abstractly govern the case endings of others.
concepts.notes: Ibn Mada's Andalusi critique famously rejected hidden governors.

concepts.name: Basran–Kufan grammatical disputes
concepts.definition: The canonical set of disagreements between the two earliest grammatical schools.

concepts.name: I'rab (case and mood inflection)
concepts.definition: The system of grammatical endings marking nouns and verbs in Arabic.

concepts.name: Sama' and qiyas in grammar
concepts.definition: Debate over whether grammatical rules rest on attested usage or systematic analogy.

concepts.name: 'Illa (grammatical causation)
concepts.definition: The theoretical justifications explaining why grammatical rules take their form.

concepts.name: Asl and far' (root and branch)
concepts.definition: Derivational logic treating some forms as primary and others as analogically derived.

concepts.name: Fasaha (linguistic purity)
concepts.definition: The ideal of eloquent, error-free Arabic rooted in Bedouin and Qur'anic usage.

concepts.name: Al-'arabiyya al-fusha (classical standard)
concepts.definition: The idealized grammatical register codified from early poetry and Qur'an.

concepts.name: Lahn (solecism)
concepts.definition: Grammatical error in speech, whose prevention motivated the rise of grammar.

concepts.name: Lughat (tribal dialects)
concepts.definition: Recognition and documentation of variant Bedouin dialects as evidence for grammar.

concepts.name: Shawahid (evidentiary citations)
concepts.definition: Use of Qur'an, hadith, and pre-Islamic poetry as proofs for grammatical rules.

concepts.name: Hadith as grammatical evidence
concepts.definition: Dispute over whether Prophetic hadith can serve as proof texts for grammar.

concepts.name: Darura shi'riyya (poetic license)
concepts.definition: Grammatical deviations permitted to poets and catalogued by grammarians.

concepts.name: Ishtiqaq (derivation)
concepts.definition: Theory of how Arabic words derive from triliteral roots by systematic pattern.

concepts.name: Ishtiqaq akbar (greater derivation)
concepts.definition: Ibn Jinni's theory linking roots sharing any permutation of the same consonants.

concepts.name: Ta'rib (arabization of loanwords)
concepts.definition: Integration of foreign words into Arabic phonology and morphology.

concepts.name: Origin of language (tawqif vs istilah)
concepts.definition: Whether language was divinely taught to Adam or established by human convention.

concepts.name: Wad' al-lugha (linguistic positing)
concepts.definition: Theory of the original assignment of words to meanings and its authority.

concepts.name: Dalala (signification)
concepts.definition: The relation between word, concept, and referent underlying all linguistic meaning.

concepts.name: Haqiqa and majaz (literal and figurative)
concepts.definition: Distinction between a word's original meaning and extended or metaphorical uses.

concepts.name: Kinaya (allusive indirect speech)
concepts.definition: Indirect expression implying meaning beyond the literal statement.

concepts.name: Tashbih (simile)
concepts.definition: The rhetorical figure of likening one thing to another and its formal types.

concepts.name: Isti'ara (metaphor)
concepts.definition: Theory of metaphor as transference of a term from its original to a resembling referent.

concepts.name: Majaz mursal (metonymy)
concepts.definition: Figurative substitution based on a non-similarity relation such as cause or part.

concepts.name: Balagha (eloquence)
concepts.definition: The overarching science of effective, contextually fitting speech.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-ma'ani (science of meanings)
concepts.definition: Study of how syntactic choices convey intended meanings in context.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-bayan (science of clarity)
concepts.definition: Branch of rhetoric studying simile, metaphor, and metonymy as modes of expression.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-badi' (rhetorical embellishment)
concepts.definition: Catalogue of verbal and semantic ornaments decorating eloquent speech.

concepts.name: Nazm (theory of syntactic composition)
concepts.definition: Al-Jurjani's doctrine that meaning arises from the ordered arrangement of words.
concepts.notes: Central innovation of classical Arabic literary theory.

concepts.name: I'jaz al-Qur'an (linguistic inimitability)
concepts.definition: Theories explaining the Qur'an's unmatched eloquence as proof of its divine origin.

concepts.name: Sarfa (deflection theory of inimitability)
concepts.definition: The view that Arabs were divinely prevented from matching the Qur'an, not its form itself.

concepts.name: Tafsir lughawi (linguistic exegesis)
concepts.definition: Qur'anic exegesis grounded primarily in lexicon, grammar, and rhetoric.

concepts.name: Gharib al-Qur'an (rare Qur'anic vocabulary)
concepts.definition: Genre explaining uncommon or obscure words in the Qur'an.

concepts.name: Mushkil al-Qur'an (problematic passages)
concepts.definition: Genre resolving apparent grammatical or semantic difficulties in the Qur'an.

concepts.name: Wujuh wa naza'ir (polysemy in Qur'an)
concepts.definition: Cataloguing multiple meanings of a single Qur'anic term across passages.

concepts.name: Qira'at (canonical readings)
concepts.definition: The transmitted variant recitations of the Qur'anic text and their linguistic analysis.

concepts.name: Tajwid (rules of recitation)
concepts.definition: The phonetic discipline governing proper articulation of Qur'anic recitation.

concepts.name: Makharij al-huruf (articulation points)
concepts.definition: Classification of Arabic consonants by their precise points of articulation.

concepts.name: Sifat al-huruf (phonetic qualities)
concepts.definition: Description of consonantal features like voicing, emphasis, and manner of articulation.

concepts.name: Imala (vowel fronting)
concepts.definition: Phonetic phenomenon inclining long 'a' toward 'e', regulated in recitation and dialect.

concepts.name: Idgham (assimilation)
concepts.definition: Merging adjacent identical or similar consonants in pronunciation.

concepts.name: 'Arud (prosody)
concepts.definition: Al-Khalil's metrical analysis of Arabic poetry into sixteen canonical meters.

concepts.name: Qafiya (rhyme theory)
concepts.definition: The formal analysis of rhyme structures and their faults in Arabic poetry.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-shi'r (poetic theory)
concepts.definition: Theoretical reflection on the nature, purposes, and criticism of poetry.

concepts.name: Takhyil (poetic imagination)
concepts.definition: Aristotelian-inspired theory that poetry moves the soul through imaginative assent.

concepts.name: Sariqat shi'riyya (poetic plagiarism)
concepts.definition: The critical analysis of how later poets borrow motifs and phrases from predecessors.

concepts.name: Lafz and ma'na (word and meaning)
concepts.definition: Debate over whether eloquence resides in wording, meaning, or their composition.

concepts.name: Grammar versus logic debate
concepts.definition: The famous dispute over whether logic or Arabic grammar better captures meaning.
concepts.notes: The 932 CE Baghdad debate between al-Sirafi and Matta is foundational.

concepts.name: Logic of language in usul
concepts.definition: Usul al-fiqh's analysis of command, prohibition, general, and particular as linguistic categories.

concepts.name: 'Amm and khass as linguistic forms
concepts.definition: Analysis of general and particular expressions and their default semantic scope.

concepts.name: Mushtarak (homonymy)
concepts.definition: Words sharing a single form but carrying multiple unrelated meanings.

concepts.name: Taraduf (synonymy)
concepts.definition: Debate over whether true synonyms exist in Arabic or every word carries distinct nuance.

concepts.name: Furuq lughawiyya (lexical distinctions)
concepts.definition: Genre identifying subtle meaning differences between near-synonyms.

concepts.name: Addad (contranyms)
concepts.definition: Arabic words that carry two opposite meanings, catalogued as a lexical curiosity.

concepts.name: Kitab al-'ayn system
concepts.definition: Al-Khalil's phonetic ordering of the lexicon by articulation point rather than alphabet.

concepts.name: Rhyme-based lexicography
concepts.definition: Arranging dictionaries by the final radical to serve poets and rhymers.

concepts.name: Thematic lexicography
concepts.definition: Organizing vocabulary by semantic field such as camels, weapons, or weather.

concepts.name: Grammatical abridgment (mukhtasar) tradition
concepts.definition: Genre of compact didactic grammars with extensive commentary traditions.

concepts.name: Alfiyya commentary tradition
concepts.definition: Versified grammatical summas and the layered commentaries that explicate them.

concepts.name: Persian grammatical tradition
concepts.definition: Grammar and lexicography of New Persian modeled on and distinguished from Arabic.

concepts.name: Turkic lexicography
concepts.definition: Comparative documentation of Turkic dialects and vocabulary beginning with al-Kashgari.

concepts.name: Fusha and 'ammiyya (standard and vernacular)
concepts.definition: Recognition of the gap between classical Arabic and spoken dialects.

concepts.name: Saj' (rhymed prose)
concepts.definition: Ornate rhymed and rhythmic prose style characteristic of sermons and maqamat.

concepts.name: Insha' (chancery prose)
concepts.definition: The art of official epistolary composition codified in chancery manuals.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-khatt (calligraphic theory)
concepts.definition: The aesthetic and proportional theory of Arabic script and its canonical hands.

concepts.name: Rasm al-mushaf (Qur'anic orthography)
concepts.definition: The fixed consonantal spelling of the Qur'anic codex and its rules.

concepts.name: Nahda Arabic reform
concepts.definition: 19th–20th century project to modernize Arabic vocabulary and simplify grammar.
